subproblem.title: Agreement of a closed locally planar set with a 2-plane near one unit point propagates along the whole great circle
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be a closed set such that every p ∈ S with p ≠ 0 has δ > 0 and a 2-dimensional linear subspace Q' of ℝ^P with S ∩ B_δ(p) = Q' ∩ B_δ(p). Let Q be a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, and suppose some x₀ ∈ Q with |x₀| = 1 and some ε₀ > 0 satisfy S ∩ B_ε₀(x₀) = Q ∩ B_ε₀(x₀). Then every x ∈ Q with |x| = 1 has some ε > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(x) = Q ∩ B_ε(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (x₀ : Euclid P) (ε₀ : ℝ), IsClosed S → (∀ p ∈ S, p ≠ 0 → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (Q' : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < δ ∧ Module.finrank ℝ Q' = 2 ∧ S ∩ ball p δ = (Q' : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball p δ) → Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → x₀ ∈ Q → ‖x₀‖ = 1 → 0 < ε₀ → S ∩ ball x₀ ε₀ = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x₀ ε₀ → ∀ x : Euclid P, x ∈ Q → ‖x‖ = 1 → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ S ∩ ball x ε = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2-3 (points where S is locally a given plane; whole great circles) of the supplied proof of idtp_tdc_cone_set_finite_planes. Notation: B_r(y) = ball y r; 𝕊 := {y ∈ ℝ^P : |y| = 1} (Mathlib `sphere 0 1`); K := Q ∩ 𝕊; A := {y ∈ ℝ^P : there is ε > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(y) = Q ∩ B_ε(y)}. The claim to prove is K ⊆ A.
1. (K is connected.) As finrank Q = 2, Q is finite-dimensional (Module.finite_of_finrank_eq_succ) and Module.rank ℝ Q = 2 > 1 (Module.finrank_eq_rank). Q with the norm restricted from ℝ^P is a real normed space, so by Mathlib's isConnected_sphere (file Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Connected.lean; that module is not imported by the frozen header, so the implementation adds the pinned import `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected` to Submission.lean, exactly as accepted Ch07 commits such as bff81d31e added other pinned Mathlib imports) the unit sphere {z ∈ Q : |z| = 1} of Q is connected. Its image under the continuous inclusion Q → ℝ^P (Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val) is exactly K: an element z of Q has the same norm in Q and in ℝ^P, and every y ∈ K is the image of ⟨y, y ∈ Q⟩. A continuous image of a connected set is connected (IsConnected.image), so K is connected, in particular preconnected.
2. (A is open.) Let y ∈ A, with ε > 0 and S ∩ B_ε(y) = Q ∩ B_ε(y), and let y' ∈ B_ε(y), d := |y' − y| < ε. Put ε' := ε − d > 0. Then B_ε'(y') ⊆ B_ε(y) because ε' + d ≤ ε (Metric.ball_subset_ball'), so S ∩ B_ε'(y') = (S ∩ B_ε(y)) ∩ B_ε'(y') = (Q ∩ B_ε(y)) ∩ B_ε'(y') = Q ∩ B_ε'(y'), i.e. y' ∈ A. Hence B_ε(y) ⊆ A, and A is open (Metric.isOpen_iff).
3. (A ∩ Q ⊆ S.) If y ∈ A ∩ Q, with ε as in the definition of A, then y ∈ Q ∩ B_ε(y) = S ∩ B_ε(y), so y ∈ S.
4. (Points of K outside A are not in the closure of A ∩ Q.) Let x ∈ K with x ∉ A. We find r > 0 such that no y ∈ A ∩ Q satisfies |x − y| < r; by Metric.mem_closure_iff this means x ∉ closure(A ∩ Q).
 (a) Case x ∉ S. S is closed, so its complement is open and some r > 0 has B_r(x) ∩ S = ∅. If some y ∈ A ∩ Q had |x − y| < r, then y ∈ S by step 3 and y ∈ B_r(x), a contradiction.
 (b) Case x ∈ S. Since |x| = 1, x ≠ 0, so the local-planarity hypothesis gives δ > 0 and a subspace Q' with S ∩ B_δ(x) = Q' ∩ B_δ(x) (the dimension of Q' is not used). Then Q' ≠ Q, since Q' = Q would put x in A (with ε := δ). Take r := δ/2 and suppose y ∈ A ∩ Q with |x − y| < δ/2, witnessed by ε_y > 0 with S ∩ B_ε_y(y) = Q ∩ B_ε_y(y). Let τ := min(ε_y, δ/2) > 0. Then B_τ(y) ⊆ B_ε_y(y), and B_τ(y) ⊆ B_δ(x) because τ + |y − x| < δ/2 + δ/2 = δ. Consequently
 Q ∩ B_τ(y) = (Q ∩ B_ε_y(y)) ∩ B_τ(y) = (S ∩ B_ε_y(y)) ∩ B_τ(y) = S ∩ B_τ(y) = (S ∩ B_δ(x)) ∩ B_τ(y) = (Q' ∩ B_δ(x)) ∩ B_τ(y) = Q' ∩ B_τ(y).
 Since y ∈ Q and τ > 0, the sibling theorem idtp_tdc_csfp_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball (applied to P, Q, Q', y, τ) gives Q = Q', contradicting Q' ≠ Q.
5. (Connectedness.) Let u := A and v := ℝ^P ∖ closure(A ∩ Q); both are open (step 2; complement of a closed set). Every point of K lies in u or, by step 4, in v; so K ⊆ u ∪ v. K ∩ u is nonempty: x₀ ∈ Q and |x₀| = 1 give x₀ ∈ K, and ε₀ > 0 with S ∩ B_ε₀(x₀) = Q ∩ B_ε₀(x₀) gives x₀ ∈ A. Suppose some x ∈ K is not in A. Then x ∈ v by step 4, so K ∩ v ≠ ∅, and preconnectedness of K (step 1; the definition of IsPreconnected applied to u, v) yields z ∈ K ∩ (u ∩ v). But z ∈ K ⊆ Q and z ∈ A, so z ∈ A ∩ Q ⊆ closure(A ∩ Q) (subset_closure), contradicting z ∈ v. Therefore K ⊆ A.
6. (Conclusion.) Let x ∈ Q with |x| = 1. Then x ∈ K ⊆ A, i.e. there is ε > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(x) = Q ∩ B_ε(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: The great circle K = Q ∩ 𝕊 is connected: it is the image under the inclusion Q → ℝ^P of the unit sphere of the 2-dimensional normed space Q (isConnected_sphere, IsConnected.image).
The set A of points near which S coincides with Q is open, and A ∩ Q ⊆ S.

A point of K outside A has a ball disjoint from A ∩ Q: by closedness of S if the point is not in S, and otherwise by local planarity at the point together with idtp_tdc_csfp_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball.
Preconnectedness of K applied to the open sets A and ℝ^P ∖ closure(A ∩ Q), with the seed x₀ ∈ K ∩ A, gives K ⊆ A.
